abandon_criterion.note: one screen depth; a survivor is gated, not deepened, in this probe

bar.note: the stabilizer entry with the best kd^2/n at n <= 40; the stabilizer board ranks apart from the CSS board

direction.expected_value: A nondominated stabilizer child at d >= 3 would show that the calculus's moves transfer beyond CSS presentations and give the stabilizer board, which carries no certified distance, a frontier point with an auditable parent.
direction.feasibility: 54 stabilizer parents at n <= 40; a Pauli-weight RIS screen at 1000 trials reads a child in well under a second at these sizes, the gate accepts stabilizer documents, and the board's stabilizer entries all carry layouts or none, so children inherit what their parent has.
direction.hypothesis: Single-step symplectic moves (delete a generator, puncture a qubit, peel a qubit with one of its generators) on the board's stabilizer entries with n <= 40 reach stabilizer-board frontier points that code-calculus v0.1's CSS-only moves cannot express.

novelty.against: the stabilizer board's 226 entries, mostly codetables.de additive codes read as symplectic rows
novelty.claim: a stabilizer code one symplectic move from a board stabilizer entry, nondominated on the stabilizer board

direction.what_a_negative_would_teach: That one deletion, puncture, or peel from a stabilizer entry with n <= 40 lands only on dominated points or at d <= 2, so the stabilizer board's small-n frontier is not reachable by its own entries' single-step children and a symplectic extension of the calculus would need depth or a different move set to pay.

campaign.name: code-calculus moves on stabilizer parents (issue #4478, direction 1)
campaign.notes: Symplectic analogs of C-DELETE-CHECK, E-PUNCTURE, and E-PEEL applied once to each stabilizer board entry; see the fieldnote of 2026-11-05.
